See also: súrra

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
surra
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Marathi [script needed] (sūra, “air breathed through the nostrils”), imitative of heavy breathing through the nostrils.

Noun

[edit]

surra (uncountable)

  1. A disease of vertebrate animals caused by protozoan trypanosomes, involving fever, weakness, and lethargy.
    • 1901 May 24, “Veterinary Work at Uganda”, in The Agricultural Journal and Mining Record‎[1], volume 4, number 6, page 178:
      Whether the disease caused was Surra or Ngana time would not permit me to judge […]

Translations

[edit]
disease of animals
  • French: surra (fr) f
  • German: Surra f
  • Italian: surra f
  • Polish: surra (pl) f

Estonian

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

surra

  1. Da-infinitive of surema.

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *surdak (“to die”) (compare Estonian surema (“to die”)), from Proto-Uralic *śure- (“to die”). The modern meaning is by contamination from surku; the original meaning is still found in the derivative surma (“killing”). May also be related to Erzya сырьмай (sïŕmaj, “death”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsurːɑˣ/, [ˈs̠urːɑ̝(ʔ)]
  • Rhymes: -urːɑ
  • Syllabification(key): sur‧ra
  • Hyphenation(key): sur‧ra

Verb

[edit]

surra

  1. (intransitive) to mourn, grieve (often because of someone's death)
  2. (transitive, usually atelic) to mourn, grieve ((over) someone dead)

Ingrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *surdak (“to die”). Cognates include Finnish surra and Estonian surra.

The sense "to die" is a semantic loan from a Southern Finnic language, either Estonian surra or Votic surrõ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Ala-Laukaa) IPA(key): /ˈsurːɑ/, [ˈs̠urː]
  • (Soikkola) IPA(key): /ˈsurːɑ/, [ˈʃurːɑ]
  • Rhymes: -urː, -urːɑ
  • Hyphenation: sur‧ra

Verb

[edit]

surra

  1. (intransitive) to mourn; grieve
  2. (intransitive) to die; pass away
  3. (transitive, usually atelic) to mourn; grieve

Swedish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Of imitative origin, see also Danish sur.

Verb

[edit]

surra (present surrar, preterite surrade, supine surrat, imperative surra)

  1. to buzz (make a buzzing sound, of for example bees)
    surrande bin
    buzzing bees
  2. to talk, to buzz (often of many people)
    Vad surrar ni om?
    What are you talking about?
  3. to buzz (of rumors or the like)
    Rykten surrade i stan
    Rumors were buzzing about town
  4. (sometimes with fast) to secure (for example cargo) with a rope
    Surra lasten, en storm är på väg
    Secure the cargo, a storm is coming
